scope: Directed and repeated WITHOUT ROWID primary fields, actual column/collation duplicate suppression, secondary primary-key locator directions and limited full covering scans. Finite admitted examples, not global SQLite planner equivalence.

negative_results.reason: Descending primary declarations were rejected, and repeated key fields were either collapsed by column alone or not normalized by actual column/collation identity.

negative_results.stage: Directed physical records and repeated fields
negative_results.reason: Data and detailed metadata match. One full covering index changes SQLite's default SELECT scan order in both file modes; the implementation still scanned the primary table.

implementation: CoreAutoIndexSpec.Key retains actual direction. WITHOUT ROWID primary specifications suppress repeated column/collation identities while preserving the first direction; distinct collations keep separate fields. The existing INTEGER-PK conversion order remains intact.
The actual certified automatic origin supplies primary directions to prepared metadata. Generated expression SQL supplies values only; no direction is inferred from runtime values or oracle output.

CoreIndexKey.compareDirected compares each actual collation field with its stored direction. Table ordering, independent acquisition, record encoding and secondary primary-key suffix ordering consume the same actual direction metadata.

Logical table decoding validates every stored occurrence against the actual declared column with read affinity only. A differing repeated field cannot disappear when logicalValues selects the first occurrence.

CoreWithoutRowidRead admits unfiltered/unordered/non-distinct single-source full covering records no wider in fields than the primary record, selecting the smallest admitted full covering record with reverse-creation tie order. Actual selected index rows enter a private read materialization. This limited admission does not claim SQLite's complete planner or arbitrary statistics.

The maintained group checks actual descending/collated PK order, distinct repeated physical fields, every-field decode validation and retained secondary fields. The public comparison that exposed default scan order remains unordered, with no result post-sorting. C is unchanged.

evaluation_protocols.public_file_modes: 7856 full file observations, including 48 new directed/repeated-key cases with fresh values and both modes, plus the prior 104 WITHOUT ROWID cases. Native-origin files, creation, updates, replacement, shared columns, collation fields and metadata are compared with complete typed snapshots.
evaluation_protocols.same_connection: 348 continuing API cases pass unchanged as separate metrics; the newly added 48 cases are public file comparisons, not additional API cases.
evaluation_protocols.crashes: 516 finite SIGKILL timing samples, including 24 new descending-primary/secondary-locator cases. Production recovery followed by independent native catalog, typed values, integrity and index-key observations. No every-syscall or power-loss claim.
evaluation_protocols.named_features: The original finite named survey remains 88/88; this is not a global SQLite compatibility percentage.

proof_scope: The full build and 413 maintained Lean groups pass with required audits. The audited compareDirected_single law matches the actual comparator, including descending argument reversal. Existing source-aware checked-image/applied-write/recovery contracts consume the directed table/index validation. No global primary-key/SQL/planner equivalence theorem is claimed.
limitations: Non-ABORT declaration policies, inline primary direction syntax, UTF-16 WITHOUT ROWID acquisition/writes, auxiliary foreign-parent/planner admission, recursive auxiliary REPLACE with DELETE programs, ALTER/UPSERT and wider expression/phase combinations remain work.

Covering scan admission is limited to the stated simple full-coverage shape and field-count criterion; arbitrary WHERE/order/distinct/group shapes, planner costs/statistics and wider native planner choices are not claimed.
Bulk physical root-page layout is not globally SQLite-identical; pending new-object schema metadata and larger root-preservation cases remain separate work.
Wider error codes/phases, FAIL/IGNORE/ROLLBACK controls, triggered UPSERT, INSTEAD OF/temp triggers, writable CTEs, trigger-aware ALTER and deferred private-function declarations remain work.

UTF-16 writes/setters, native-key/materialization limits, pending new physical allocations and earlier SQL/storage limitations remain. The finite process-kill samples do not establish every syscall/power-loss schedule.
